newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares up on inflation data, seen holding gains.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares up on inflation data, seen holding gains.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices rise on weak inflation data
New Zealand share prices rose on Tuesday after key Consumer Price inflation data came in lower than market expectations, promting a rally in wholesale interest rates.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index, up about 15 points prior to the March quarter CPI release, rallied a further 10 points to 2,252.83.
Statistics New Zealand said the CPI fell 0.3 percent in the March quarter for a 1.8 percent annualised rise.

The Reserve Bank later calculated that underlying inflation was 0.22 percent for the quarter and 1.97 for the year, against economists' expectations of a 0.41 percent rise for the quarter and a 2.16 percent rise for the year.
By 11.50 a.m., an hour after the 10.45 a.m. (2245 GMT) CPI release, the top-40 index had settling at 2,250.24, up 23.14 points or 1.04 percent.
"It's come in a lot better than most commentators expected," Peter Lynds at ANZ Securities said of the CPI. "Certainly the market re-rated pretty quickly."
